equity_bridge.item: Bajaj Holdings & Investment Ltd quoted stake, 3,500,000 shares at fair value (FVOCI)
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR note 5B l.9543-9545, Rs 3,061.10 crore at 31 Mar 2026 (Rs 4,365.57 crore a year earlier). Its Rs 32.55 crore dividend is excluded from the flows, so the asset enters the bridge at value (matching-asset rule). ~Rs 111/share.

equity_bridge.item: Investments in subsidiaries at carrying cost (KTM chain via BAIH BV Rs 2,421 crore, Bajaj Auto Credit Rs 2,700 crore, Bajaj Auto Technology Rs 470 crore, others Rs 113 crore) plus Rs 500 crore 8% BACL subordinated debentures
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 AR note 5A l.9511-9536 Total (A) Rs 5,703.88 crore; debentures l.9577-9578. Carried at cost with no impairment. Book is conservative for BACL (Rs 665 crore PAT, 23% ROE on ~Rs 3,200 crore of capital) and a judgment for the restructured KTM stake; the Rs 1,636 crore of intra-group loans is excluded. ~Rs 226/share in total.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_7yr_cagr_fy2019_fy2026 -- the GST-clean, through-cycle window (export downturn, COVID trough, FY2024-26 recovery); the base path decelerates through it by year 2
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.8% diverges >30% from revenue 16.2% and EPS 17.4%. Equity growth is suppressed by Rs 8,040 crore of buybacks FY2023-FY2025 and payouts of 70-100% of PAT, not by weak earnings; it is not used as the growth anchor. The 3yr/5yr windows (FY2021/FY2023 bases) start from the COVID trough and the pre-recovery export slump and overstate sustainable growth, which is why the 7-year window anchors the path.
historical_growth.notes: All CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income is already outside reported FCF under Ind AS presentation). Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are identical to 0.1pp because SBC is 0.02-0.12% of revenue. FY2017-FY2018 excluded from every window (excise-to-GST revenue presentation break). Base-year inputs in INR millions: revenue 587,324.8; EBITDA 120,166.1 (20.5%); D&A 4,482.1 (0.76%); capex 5,010.9 (0.85%); SBC 706.0; income-tax paid 30,855.8; reported FCF 84,601.5; PAT 98,246.6.

scenario_narratives.base: The GST-cut volume step-up holds, domestic motorcycle growth normalises to mid-single digits after FY2027 while Bajaj's share stabilises around 15-16% on the refreshed Pulsar/125cc+ range; exports keep compounding from the FY2026 rebound (2.25m units) as LatAm, Africa and the Philippines/Nepal recover; e3W (WEGO/Riki) extends the ~74% ICE three-wheeler franchise into electric. EBITDA margin drifts from the record 20.5% back to a 19.5% mid-cycle as the USD/INR realisation tailwind fades and EV mix dilutes, offset by premiumisation. Capex steps up to ~1.5% of revenue for Chakan-II and EV capacity. Revenue roughly doubles over ten years (FY2036 ~Rs 1.24 lakh crore); terminal value binds on Gordon (12% / 5%), i.e. 15x final-year FCF.
scenario_narratives.bull: Exports sustain 20%+ growth for several years (Africa >2x, Nigeria 3x, CV exports +70% in Q1 FY27 as the base), Chetak and e3W scale with supply constraints lifted and reach ICE-parity margins, premiumisation plus 'dynamic P&L management' hold margin at 21% through the cycle, and the domestic 125cc+ interventions win share back. Standalone revenue reaches ~Rs 1.47 lakh crore by FY2036. This case needs several independent things to go right (export macro, EV margins, domestic share), which is why it is weighted below the house default.
scenario_narratives.bear: The GST-driven demand pull-forward fades in FY2028-29 (Bernstein-style ~2% industry growth), domestic motorcycle share keeps slipping toward 14% as Hero, TVS and Honda press the commuter and 125-160cc segments, an export-market currency or financing shock (Nigeria/LatAm-style) interrupts the rebound, and commodity inflation plus the PM eDrive subsidy phase-out compress margins to the FY2019-23 17.5% level. Capex still rises for EV capacity so FCF conversion weakens. Terminal growth 4% and a 15x cap reflect a slower, more cyclical franchise. Not modelled in the standalone flows but a reason for the elevated bear weight: a second KTM capital call or BACL asset-quality problem would be funded from the same cash pile that sits in the bridge.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A debt-free, high-ROIC two- and three-wheeler franchise with a large, genuinely liquid fixed-income surplus and a near-monopoly in Indian three-wheelers, valued on the standalone owner FCF it actually produces, discounted at an INR cost of equity, with the record FY2026 margin mid-cycled and the investment book, the listed Bajaj Holdings stake and the subsidiaries' carrying value added once in the bridge. The gap between the house value and the market price is almost entirely the discount rate: Indian quality cyclicals trade at 25-30x earnings, which equates to a ~9-10% INR required return against the 12% used here. The required-return table and the WACC x g grid are the honest statement of that gap; the subsidiaries (KTM, BACL) are an upside option the standalone model deliberately carries at book.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount-rate calibration: at a 10% INR cost of equity the base value is materially higher -- the valuation is a terminal-value-heavy, rate-sensitive answer and the sensitivity grid is the primary disclosure
FY2026 margin may be above mid-cycle by more than the 1pp fade assumed (FX realisation, GST timing, PM eDrive subsidy phase-out on e3W margins)
Domestic motorcycle share erosion (16.6% -> 15.6% in FY2026) continuing into the 125cc+ core
Export cyclicality and EM currency shocks (Nigeria, LatAm) reversing the FY2026-27 rebound

Subsidiary cash calls: a further KTM/Bajaj Mobility capital need or BACL credit cycle would be funded from the surplus counted in the bridge; subsidiaries are carried at book, which could be either conservative (BACL) or too generous (KTM)
Q2 FY2027 results (Oct 2026) are not in the data set; FY2027 year-1 growth is judged from Q1 alone

data_sources.financials: research/BAJAJ-AUTO.NS/Reports/BAJAJ-AUTO.NS_Metrics.csv (standalone, INR millions, FY2012-FY2026 + quarterlies); FY2026 Annual Report standalone statements (balance sheet l.7755-7829, cash flow l.8051-8204, investments notes 5A/5B l.9500-9800); Q1 FY2027 press release (21 Jul 2026); kpis table (cash taxes, D&A, interest income, buybacks, volumes)

inputs.share_count_basis: 279,497,838 shares at 31 Mar 2026 (FY2026 AR, Directors' Report l.2045) less 4,694,000 shares bought back by tender offer at Rs 12,000 (record date 24 Jun 2026, offer opened 1 Jul 2026, FY2026 AR l.2024-2030) = 274,803,838. Diluted EPS equals basic EPS (Rs 351.5) to one decimal, so ESOP dilution is <0.1% and the ESOP trust settles options from treasury shares; count held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows.

net_cash_composition_inr_crore.source: FY2026 AR standalone balance sheet l.7764-7829; note 5B l.9539-9800; buyback and dividend l.2023-2030 and l.545-546. Company's own 'surplus cash and cash equivalents' was Rs 18,137 crore at 31 Mar 2026 (l.540) and 'over Rs 21,000 crore' at 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 FY27 PR) -- both pre-buyback and pre-final-dividend; our Rs 22,048 crore gross figure exceeds management's because it counts all rated fixed-income holdings at balance-sheet value. Intra-group loans (Rs 1,635.71 crore non-current, largely EUR loans into the BAIH BV / KTM chain) are excluded entirely. FCF generated since 1 Apr 2026 (Rs 2,300+ crore in Q1 FY27 alone) is NOT added to cash because it is inside the FY2027 year-1 projection.

inputs.interest_income_note: Ind AS indirect-method cash flow: the Rs 1,336.76 crore of FY2026 investment income (interest on fixed income, ETFs, FMPs, MF fair-value gains, dividends on strategic investments) is REMOVED from operating activities and shown in investing (FY2026 AR l.8084-8096, l.8145-8154). Reported OCF Rs 8,961 crore and hence reported FCF already exclude it, so deducting it again would double-strip. EBITDA (Rs 12,017 crore, 20.5%) is operating EBITDA excluding other income. The matching asset (the investment book) is in net_debt / equity_bridge. Residual conservatism: income-tax paid inside OCF includes ~Rs 300 crore of tax on that investment income.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR standalone cash flow statement l.8072 'Share based payment to employees' Rs 70.60 crore (FY2025 Rs 64.87 crore). No net-share-settlement tax line exists (ESOP trust settles from treasury shares); EquityAwardTaxes = 0.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 financing outflow for buyback was nil; FY2025 Rs 931.84 crore, FY2024 Rs 4,017 crore, FY2023 Rs 3,094 crore. The Rs 5,633 crore July-2026 tender buyback is a post-balance-sheet event handled in net_debt and shares_outstanding above, not here. Flat count is funded: the company is a repurchaser and SBC is 0.12% of revenue.
inputs.latest_quarter_in_hand: Q1 FY2027 (quarter to 30 Jun 2026, PR dated 21 Jul 2026): revenue Rs 17,244 crore +37% YoY, EBITDA 20.9%, PAT Rs 2,983 crore, FCF Rs 2,300+ crore. Q2 FY2027 (Sept 2026 quarter) results are not in the Extracted folder.
inputs.wacc_rationale: INR flows discounted at an INR cost of equity: India 10-year G-sec ~6.4% (RBI repo 5.25% by Apr 2026 per FY2026 AR), India ERP ~6.5% (mature-market 4.3% plus country risk), beta ~0.85 for a net-cash two-wheeler OEM -> cost of equity ~11.9%, rounded to 12.0%. Zero debt so WACC = cost of equity. Same WACC in all three scenarios (risk is charged once, in the flows). Terminal growth 5.0% nominal INR (RBI 4% inflation target plus ~1% real) -- a lower bar than India's ~10% nominal GDP growth. NOT a USD-built rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: None required: the standalone balance sheet carries no lease liabilities or right-of-use assets (lease liabilities of Rs 469 crore appear only in the consolidated statements, l.13240, and belong to KTM/BACL). D&A of Rs 448 crore is owned PP&E.
inputs.nci_treatment: Not applicable on the standalone basis: 100% of standalone profit is attributable. The 25.06% public minority in Bajaj Mobility AG (KTM) sits outside this model.
inputs.scope_note: Values the STANDALONE auto business (motorcycles, three-wheelers, EVs, spares; India plus exports). Subsidiaries -- KTM via Bajaj Auto International Holdings BV (74.94% of Bajaj Mobility AG since Nov 2025, restructured in 2025), Bajaj Auto Credit (NBFC, AUM Rs 18,835 crore, PAT Rs 665 crore FY2026) and Bajaj Auto Technology -- are NOT consolidated into the flows; they enter only as the Rs 5,704 crore carrying value of investments in subsidiaries plus Rs 500 crore BACL debentures in equity_bridge. Per-share value of that bridge item is ~Rs 226; zero it to see the pure standalone number.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (FY2027-FY2036), scenario-weighted -- routed via dcf-methods as a non-US, moderately cyclical operating company (owner-fcf.md plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md: INR WACC, no leases, no NCI, matching-asset rule for the investment book, SBC near-zero). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model. Base-year choice: FY2026 revenue (Rs 58,732 crore, +17%) is kept as FY0 because the Sept-2025 GST cut (28%->18% on <=350cc) is a permanent price reduction that lifts the volume base rather than a one-off, and Q1 FY2027 ran +37% on top of it; the record 20.5% EBITDA margin (20.9% in Q1 FY27, helped by favourable USD/INR realisation) IS mid-cycled -- the FY2019-FY2023 range was 16.5-18.0% and FY2024-26 19.7-20.5% -- fading to 19.5% in the base and 17.5% in the bear. Revenue growth FY2017-FY2018 is distorted by the excise-to-GST transition (pre-July-2017 revenue was gross of excise) and is excluded from every CAGR window used. Cash tax 25.2% = Sec 115BAA statutory rate; the FY2026 cash rate of 23.6% of PBT is lower only because investment income is taxed at concessional rates. Working-capital capture 0%: the business runs negative working capital (payables Rs 7,356 crore > receivables Rs 2,712 crore + inventory Rs 2,354 crore) so growth releases cash, but the FY2025/FY2026 changes were -Rs 243 crore / +Rs 105 crore, so no credit is taken.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +14%: Q1 ran +37% but H2 FY2026 already carried the GST-cut volume step-up, so H2 FY2027 compares against a high base; exports (+54% volumes in Q1) are the swing factor. Thereafter decelerates through the 9.9% through-cycle revenue CAGR to 5% by FY2036.
base.margin_rationale: Record 20.5% mid-cycled to 19.5%: FX realisation tailwind fades, EV mix (30% of domestic revenue, margin-dilutive) rises, commodity inflation flagged by management; offset by premiumisation and operating leverage.
base.capex_rationale: Step-up from 0.85% of revenue (Rs 501 crore) to 1.5% (~Rs 1,000 crore) for Chakan-II, Chetak and e3W capacity -- management guided capex up qualitatively; D&A follows with a lag.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because FY0 sits at a cyclical and policy-aided high (record margin, GST-cut volume boost, favourable FX), because the standalone number is exposed to subsidiaries that can call on its cash (KTM restructured in 2025, BACL doubling AUM), and because domestic share has fallen for a year. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it requires exports, EV margins and domestic share to all improve together. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
